text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall (eng-oncall). P1 - degraded latency for runtime-serving in us-west-2. Error rate spike 12:08 UTC, elevated queue length on model-router. Auto-alerting to primary. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/2425009999

alyssa: oncall here, picking up :wave:. Primary for this shift. Quick summary: multiple clients reporting 5-10s tail latencies, some token timeouts. I see elevated retry counts on the runtime router and several 502s from backend pool.

alyssa: immediate ask - who should own initial scope: runtime (model-serving) or infra (node/network)? I'm leaning runtime-first but want infra in parallel if node-level OOMs or AZ networking.

jordan: infra-oncall. Recommending split triage: if K8s node metrics show CPU/GPU saturation or OOMs, infra owns node scale or instance replacement. If requests are getting 5xx from the model process (llm-runner) then runtime owns. Quick checks: `kubectl top nodes`, `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide`, and check autoscaler events.

jordan: runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p1-runtime-deg. Also check ASG health in aws console -> AutoScalingGroups -> redwood-runtime-usw2. If autoscaler has failed to scale for >5m, that's infra.

alyssa: doing the checks now. Pasting snippets.

alyssa: ```
# top nodes
NODE           CPU(%)   MEM(%)
ip-10-0-1-23   92%      76%
ip-10-0-2-44   31%      45%
```

alyssa: node ip-10-0-1-23 looks saturated on CPU. `kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-23` shows evictions backlog and some pods with `OOMKilled` last hour.

jordan: ok that points infra. I'll start scaling action and check instance health. On it.

sophia: security-oncall here. Unless you see auth failures, token errors, or suspicious lateral activity, we won't need to block access. If you do, ping `security-oncall` and paste any suspicious logs. Also helpful: run `grep -i "auth" /var/log/runner.log` for anomalies.

mike: support. Logged 3 enterprise customers with elevated error rates. Can you collect per-customer error rates + request samples? I need to draft customer-facing comms. Also need ETA for mitigation to include in notes.

alyssa: mike - grabbing customer metrics. Current sample: `customer: AcmeCorp - 14% 5xx over 15m, avg latency 6.2s`. I'll attach more in a follow-up.

oncall-rotations: FYI - secondary (APAC) is out until 18:00 UTC due to travel. Coverage gap noted. If this escalates, please escalate to infra lead (jordan) or to oncall fallback list: `@jordan`, `@dev-leads`.

oncall-rotations: also posting manual handoff snippet you can paste into the incident timeline: `Primary: alyssa (current). Secondary: none (APAC OOO). Escalation: infra-oncall (jordan).`

jordan: scaled the ASG by +2 instances, draining node ip-10-0-1-23. Linking autoscaler event: https://cloud.redwood.internal/asg/events/ev-3245. Expect new nodes in ~2-3m.

alyssa: draining in progress. I'm rerouting small subset of traffic to canary router to reduce pressure: `curl -X POST /admin/router/split -d '{"canary":0.05}'` (internal only).

mike: thanks. For customer comms: set initial ETA to 10-15m pending node replacement and draining. I'll notify AcmeCorp + BetaWorks.

sophia: seen any auth-related 403s?

alyssa: no 403 spikes, mostly 502/504 and `runner: stderr: OOM` traces.

jordan: new nodes are in service. Autoscaler reported successful launch. Still seeing some backlog in the request queue for the model-router though. Could be warmup/kv-cache miss. Runtime team should investigate model-container warmup and KV cache fill times.

alyssa: assigning runtime track to @runtime-oncall. If someone from runtime can take a look at KV cache metrics and model init latency that'd be great.

runtime-oncall (via DM): I'll chime in — looking at model logs now. Seeing `cache-miss` spikes at the same window. Also seeing increased GC pauses in the model process.

alyssa: thanks. Prep notes for postmortem: suspected root cause = sudden traffic spike hitting a single saturated node -> node OOMs -> autoscaler eventually replaced nodes -> runtime cold-cache + GC pauses led to elevated 5xx.

jordan: mitigation actions performed: scaled ASG +2, drained unhealthy node, verified replacement. infra action items: investigate why autoscaler didn't pre-scale; check cloudwatch metrics and scale policy thresholds.

mike: customer comms sent (initial): "We're investigating and mitigating; expected improvement in ~15m. We'll follow up with details and postmortem."

oncall-rotations: handoff reminder for next shift (18:00 UTC): primary will be `taylor`. Alyssa please paste a 2-line summary for the manual handoff doc.

alyssa: manual handoff summary: "P1 runtime degradation in us-west-2. Cause: node OOM -> autoscaler replaced nodes; runtime cold-cache increased 5xx. Mitigations: scaled ASG +2, drained bad node, rerouted 5% traffic to canary. Next: runtime to optimize cache warmup, infra to validate autoscaler thresholds, support to update customers."

sophia: security: no action needed. Will monitor.

alyssa: closing loop: latency improving, 5xx rate trending down. I'll stay on post until handoff. If things regress, escalate to infra lead (jordan) and paging list.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by alyssa. Status -> mitigated (monitoring).
